- Published
A seven-year-old boy has been rescued from the rubble of a residential building in Dymer after 14 hours, in overnight Russian strikes on Dymer, in the Kyiv region, that killed nine people, Ukrainian officials have said.

articles.title_zh: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 after flipping North Carolina seat
facts_zh:
Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 after flipping North Carolina seat
- Published
The Democratic Party has won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives since 1992, after Democrat Chuck Hubbard unseated Republican Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina.
The race was called on Sunday, with Hubbard beating Foxx by 330 votes with 99% counted.
It was one of the closest contests of the recent midterm elections, in which Democrats also secured the Senate.

articles.title_original: COP31 fails to reach major climate deal as talks expose deep divisions
articles.title_zh: COP31 fails to reach major climate deal as talks expose deep divisions
facts_zh:
COP31 fails to reach major climate deal as talks expose deep divisions
- Published
Countries have failed to reach a major new deal to tackle climate change after deep divisions over fossil fuels and money emerged at the UN COP31 talks in Turkey.
Negotiations were due to finish on Friday but ran late into Sunday in search of common ground, becoming the longest UN climate conference in history.
But the final deal proved unacceptable to the EU, Pacific island nations and others because it failed to directly mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.

all_titles.en: COP31 fails to reach major climate deal as talks expose deep divisions

facts_zh:
US Army to detonate tonnes of unstable explosives in Iowa despite court order
- Published
The US Army plans to move ahead with detonating five tonnes of degraded explosives in Iowa despite a ruling to halt it indefinitely, a new court filing shows.
"To protect its personnel and the surrounding communities, the Army needs to take swift action," the justice department notified the court on Saturday.

"Protection of human health and the environment demand action now, not delay."
The court had ordered a pause after environmental groups sued to stop the detonation, arguing the army failed to consider safer alternatives.

articles.title_original: South Korea education minister resigns over exam cheating scandal
articles.title_zh: South Korea education minister resigns over exam cheating scandal
facts_zh:
South Korea education minister resigns over exam cheating scandal
- Published
South Korea's Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin has resigned over an exam cheating scandal that shocked the nation.
He said he took full responsibility for the confusion caused by last-minute measures aimed at stopping AI-assisted cheating during Thursday's annual college entrance exam, known as Suneung.
A week ago, the top scorer in the national tax accountancy exam admitted using a mini-camera, mobile phone and AI tools.

facts_zh: New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people • Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.

Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.

articles.title_original: Italian jeweller and businessman Paolo Bulgari dies aged 89
articles.title_zh: Italian jeweller and businessman Paolo Bulgari dies aged 89
facts_zh:
Italian jeweller and businessman Paolo Bulgari dies aged 89
- Published
Italian jeweller Paolo Bulgari, who helped turn his family's business into a global luxury brand, has died in Rome aged age 89.
His family announced the news, remembering him as "the greatest jeweller of our time", according to Italian media.
Paolo Bulgari was Chairman of the Bvlgari Group since 1984 and its jewellery pieces have adorned Hollywood stars and royalty including Diana, Princess of Wales.

all_titles.en: Italian jeweller and businessman Paolo Bulgari dies aged 89

articles.title_original: Fire at confectionery factory in Indonesia leaves at least three dead and dozens missing
articles.title_zh: Fire at confectionery factory in Indonesia leaves at least three dead and dozens missing
facts_zh: Relatives of the missing victims flocked to the factory’s entrance, seeking updates about their loved ones A fire at a confectionery factory west of Jakarta has killed three people with 36 remaining missing, an Indonesian rescue official says.
Drone footage showed large parts of the factory destroyed, with the roof collapsed in places and smoke still rising from the complex.
Photos and videos shared by rescuers show officers entering the charred building in search of the missing victims on Sunday, with small fires still burning in some spots.

all_titles.en: Fire at confectionery factory in Indonesia leaves at least three dead and dozens missing
